Form Accessibility Checklist for WCAG Compliance

2026-06-04 10 min read

A WCAG form accessibility checklist for labels, required fields, instructions, validation, errors, keyboard access, focus management, and successful submission.

Why Form Accessibility Directly Impacts Revenue and Compliance

Forms are where users convert—requesting quotes, booking appointments, signing up for accounts, and completing ecommerce checkouts. When a form is inaccessible, visitors literally cannot do business with you, and forms are one of the most frequently cited barriers in ADA and WCAG audits.

WCAG Criteria Every Form Must Meet

  • 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A): Labels and field groups are programmatically associated with inputs.
  • 2.4.6 Headings and Labels (Level AA): Labels clearly describe the purpose of each field.
  • 3.3.1 Error Identification (Level A): Errors are described in text, not only by turning a border red.
  • 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A): Required fields, format expectations (e.g., MM/DD/YYYY), and hints are provided upfront.
  • 3.3.3 Error Suggestion (Level AA): When an input error is detected and suggestions are known, helpful correction guidance is provided.
  • 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A): Custom checkboxes, toggles, and dropdowns expose their state to assistive technology.

The Complete Form Accessibility Checklist

  1. Always pair <label for="..."> with a matching id on every <input>, <select>, and <textarea>.
  2. Never use placeholder as a replacement for a visible <label>—placeholders disappear as soon as typing starts and often fail contrast.
  3. Group related radio buttons and checkboxes inside <fieldset> with a descriptive <legend>.
  4. Indicate required fields clearly in text (or (required)) and aria-required="true", never by an unexplained red asterisk alone.
  5. Link helper text and inline error messages to the input using aria-describedby and set aria-invalid="true" on invalid fields.
  6. Ensure error messages and submission confirmations are announced via aria-live="polite" or by moving focus to an error summary.
  7. Include autocomplete attributes (name, email, tel, street-address) to support cognitive and motor accessibility.

Accessible Form Code Example

<form novalidate>
  <div class="form-group">
    <label for="work-email">Work email (required)</label>
    <input id="work-email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required aria-required="true" aria-describedby="email-hint email-error">
    <p id="email-hint">We will send your audit summary here.</p>
    <p id="email-error" role="alert" hidden>Please enter a valid email address, such as name@company.com.</p>
  </div>
  <button type="submit">Request Free Review</button>
</form>

Common WordPress &amp; Ecommerce Form Pitfalls

Popular WordPress plugins (Contact Form 7, WPForms, Gravity Forms) and Shopify newsletter/checkout forms often ship with placeholder-only inputs, low-contrast error text, or custom select dropdowns that break keyboard navigation. See our WordPress accessibility fixes page or send us your form URL for a free teardown.
